bullets.text: June YTD CR 85.6 with strong profitability; operating results are strong and business is in excellent shape at the halfway point.
Closing in on 10M PIF covering 14M+ drivers; Drive auto PIF +~7%, Progressive Direct auto +~14%, Commercial Auto +~13%, Special Lines +16%; retention metrics improved modestly.

Through June, NPW grew 8%, below multi-year average growth rates; low accident frequency along with stabilizing or reducing rates continue, creating an environment that does not motivate consumer shopping behavior.

Current environment of stabilizing or reducing rates benefits consumers and profitability but does not motivate shopping; management observed this result last year and expects it to continue through the year.
Severity trends in most coverages are no longer entirely offset by lower frequency; management is attempting to compete smartly in current conditions and preparing for growth when shopping increases.
Announced intent to add about 50 concierge service centers over the next couple of years; opened two sites in Q2 and plans four more this year, meeting its fast, fair, better standard.

Deployments of new customer billing and claims platforms meet expectations; work is well underway on a redesigned policy management system; ground broken on Colorado Springs data center, expected operational in 2007.

Formally announced the two-brand strategy—Drive Insurance from Progressive and Progressive Direct—nine months ago; Direct aired a fresh presentation of its price comparison service in commercials throughout most of Q2.

Management is pleased with agents accepting Drive and promoting agent-related benefits; Direct business, particularly Internet-generated, saw attractive growth in soft market conditions with consumers responding to its 'easy' message.

First-half results were unaffected by major weather events, though winter lingered into May; watching a projected active hurricane season as an opportunity to execute preparedness programs and provide hallmark claims response.
